html:
Chaitanya was a Bengali saint who lived from 1486 to 1534 and founded the form of Krishna worship followed across Bengal, Odisha and Manipur. His followers hold that he was Krishna himself.

He was born at Nabadwip, then a centre of Sanskrit learning, and was a brilliant young teacher of logic. At twenty-two, on a visit to Gaya, he had a religious experience that changed him. He began to lead groups through the streets singing the names of Krishna with drums and cymbals, dancing until he fell. This public singing, kirtan, was open to all castes and to Muslims. When the town's Muslim judge banned it, Chaitanya led a crowd to his house, and the judge gave way.

In 1510 he became a wandering monk. He walked through south India and to Vrindavan, then settled at the temple town of Puri for his last eighteen years.

He wrote only eight verses. He sent six learned followers to Vrindavan to find its lost holy places and set out his teaching in books. His movement is part of the bhakti movement and shaped Bengali song and poetry down to Tagore. In 1966 a follower took it to New York as the Hare Krishna movement.
sum: Chaitanya was a Bengali saint who lived from 1486 to 1534 and founded the form of Krishna worship followed across Bengal, Odisha and Manipur. His followers hold that he was Krishna himself.
